parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the required pure Rust 2021 earcut port, exact reference output order, C atoi-like parsing, std-only constraint, /output/test2.rs and /output/earcut.rs deliverables, and byte-for-byte verification across specified cases.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent explored reference behavior, then delegated two independent complete implementation attempts: agent-0 owned the primary /output deliverable, and agent-1 owned an isolated backup in /tmp/earcut_candidate_b. The parent retained final acceptance responsibility.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 wrote a full linked-list earcut module and test2 entry point, compiled /output/test2, discovered and corrected atoi overflow behavior, and returned a detailed summary. Agent-1 separately built a similar backup and fixed its own compile errors.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: There was no component merge: the primary child wrote directly to the requested /output paths, the backup stayed outside /output, and the parent checked /output before final delivery.
parallel.verification: Agent-0 reported required cases plus an extended 105-case byte-for-byte sweep passing; agent-1 reported required and extended comparisons passing; the parent then spot-checked the /output executable against the reference for 11 cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required work was visible at closure; official status confirmed the parallel artifact passed 40 of 40 evaluated testcases.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, exact-output, atoi, file placement, and reference-binary verification requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One main agent owned the entire workflow: probing behavior, writing Cargo metadata, implementing the earcut module and entry point, compiling, testing, and reporting final status.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote Cargo.toml, /output/earcut.rs, /output/test2.rs, and compiled /output/test2 plus target/release/test2 from a single local implementation path.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial implementation was assembled directly in /output as one coherent project, with no delegated components or cross-agent integration step.
serial.verification: The serial agent compared outputs against the reference for multiple explicit cases, then separately verified the true no-argument default case and listed the generated output files.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required work was visible at closure; official status confirmed the serial artifact passed 40 of 40 evaluated testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized exact stdout strings, atoi behavior, no external crates, output paths, and broad comparison testing through its parent brief to both children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt-level obligations and locally probed the reference outputs before writing code.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement coverage gap affected the outcome; parallel repeated the full requirements in child briefs, while serial retained them in one main context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split the task into two complete implementations with distinct workspaces: primary /output and backup /tmp/earcut_candidate_b, then parent-owned final review.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation, compilation, and verification ownership inside one main-agent workflow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel duplicated the whole implementation rather than splitting components; serial avoided delegation. Both ownership plans still covered the deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent brief supplied both subagents with the reference behavior, file locations, Rust constraints, and verification list; returned handoffs agreed that their candidates passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had one continuous context and no cross-agent interface boundary, using the same prompt and local observations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child-brief and result-handoff boundaries, but they did not lose requirements or create incompatible component interfaces.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Agent-0 wrote the primary Rust earcut library and test entry point, then patched atoi overflow after extended comparison exposed a mismatch; agent-1 built a backup candidate separately.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote Cargo.toml, earcut.rs, and test2.rs directly in /output and compiled them without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented a linked-list earcut port, but parallel had two independent full candidates and a later overflow fix in the primary; serial produced one local project.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Both children completed and their summarized results returned through the AgentSwarm aggregate before the parent acted on the primary output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; its local compile and verification results were immediately available in the same trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a join point at the swarm result, but the join completed normally and the parent inspected the delivered /output candidate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run avoided component merging: agent-0 wrote /output, agent-1 wrote /tmp/earcut_candidate_b, and the parent later listed /output and tested that executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all final files into /output itself, including Cargo files and the compiled executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used isolated final and backup work locations, while serial used only the final workspace; neither trajectory shows shared-state collision affecting delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Agent-0 reported all required cases plus a 105-case sweep passing, and the parent spot-checked /output before final response; official evaluation passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reported ALL MATCH for its comparison loop, then confirmed the no-argument default separately; official evaluation passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child verification plus parent spot-check; serial had direct verification in the main trajectory. Both produced adequate acceptance evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used substantially more agent time and tokens because two complete candidates ran, but the run completed before timeout and closed after parent spot-check.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used fewer requests and tokens, completed in less agent time, and closed after direct verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was more expensive but not budget-exhausted; both closed with official completed evaluations and no unfinished deliverable.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status evaluations show both parallel and serial passed all 40 official testcases, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The process difference is that parallel duplicated the full implementation through two isolated child agents and then spot-checked the primary /output artifact, while serial solved the same task directly in one local workflow. Both produced byte-for-byte verification evidence and deliverable artifacts.
parallel_contributors: Primary child produced the requested /output deliverable and reported a 105-case byte-for-byte sweep; the parent then spot-checked the final executable.
Backup child independently produced a passing candidate in /tmp, adding confidence without requiring integration.
serial_contributors: Serial main agent retained the full context locally, wrote all requested files, compiled, and verified output matches before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel agent-0 initially had an atoi overflow mismatch during extended testing and fixed it; serial used a simpler wrapping atoi path but still matched official evaluated cases.
Serial created Cargo.toml and Cargo build artifacts while parallel primary delivered only the required files and executable in /output.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; observed differences are strategy and ordinary implementation-path differences, not retained parallel coordination errors
